newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Premier vets Discovery assets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Premier vets Discovery assets.

text.p: Premier Oil Plc said on Thursday it would begin next week to examine in detail the Australian assets of Discovery Petroleum NL.

"We have a full team arriving in Perth next week to sit down with the technical staff of Discovery to see how we are going to build the business," Premier general manager of international and new business, Steve Lowden, told Reuters in an interview.
Premier said earlier it had become entitled to more than 63 percent of the Australian oil and gas producer, and was working toward its target of 90 percent.
Lowden said Premier had a benchmark of 5,000 barrels of oil equivalent (boe) a day to justify maintaining a business.

"We would almost have to triple the size (of Australian production) to reach our own definition of an existing business," he said. "But we think at this point in time that there is potential to do just that."
About 70 percent of Discovery's income is derived from its 18.75 percent stake in Indonesia's Kakap field, which is operated by Clyde Petroleum Plc.
It also has holdings in the Perth and Carnarvon Basins, and the Timor Sea, but is producing only from its 33 percent share in Beharra Springs in the Perth Basin, operated by Boral Ltd.
Lowden said Discovery also had an interesting position in the Carnarvon Basin, which he said should provide opportunities to a company the size of Premier.
"The big oil and gas fields have been discovered and now it's on to the much more subtle and peripheral plays," he said.
Premier currently produces about 43,000 boe a day, compared with Discovery's production of about 10,000 boe a day.
Lowden said there were no plans to make big changes at Discovery.
"I don't know what our firm plans are, but there's certainly no intent to shake-up at all," he said.
"Discovery was run very lean and very efficiently and therefore it's more likely there will be a building rather than anything else," he said.
Lowden said he understood there were no major shareholders still holding a stake in Discovery.
He said he belived moving to the 90 percent compulsory takeover threshold would be a matter of logistics.
Premier's 81 cents a share offer, which values Discovery at about A$105.5 million, closes on December 23.
